rationale: The Court is likely to adopt a narrow, administrable reading that § 1109(b) is broad only after an entity qualifies as a “party in interest,” which requires a legally cognizable stake that plan confirmation can bind or alter (e.g., releases, injunctions, coverage-determinative provisions), not mere downstream economic exposure. Roberts is best positioned to write a compromise-text opinion holding insurers lack a right to object to an insurance-neutral plan, with a meaningful chance of separate dissents emphasizing statutory breadth and trial-level participation.
